term: Spreading your money across different companies, sectors, or asset types so one bad outcome doesn't sink your whole portfolio.

copy.hook: Why not put all your money in your single best stock idea?
copy.explain: Put $1,000 in one stock and it drops 50%: you have $500 left. Split it across 10 stocks and the same drop hits one: you have $950.
copy.takeaway: Diversifying won't stop losses. It caps what one mistake can cost.
copy.question: If all 10 of your stocks are tech companies, how diversified are you really?
